text:
maya: heads-up — quarterly hosted API capacity sync. forecasting a 32% q/q spike in token throughput for Oct-Dec based on current PLG funnel + new retailer integration. need decision on 3 options: short-term cloud rentals, 6-12mo leases, or partial purchase.

raj: can you post the model-level gpu-hour uplift numbers? rough is fine.

maya: sure. rough weekly GPU-hour delta (aggregate across clusters):
- baseline: 48k GPU-hours/week
- expected spike peak week: 63k GPU-hours/week (avg +32%)
- steady elevated: ~56k GPU-hours/week

liam: okay. region breakdown? where is the traffic going?

maya: mostly us-west and eu-west. apac smaller but growth is concentrated in singapore edge. can route some cross-region but latency-sensitive customers in APAC need local capacity.

elaine: budget signal from finance — capital for buys is limited this quarter. they prefer leases or on-demand, but will consider buys if ROI < 18 months.

sergio: ops constraints: cold-rack provisioning lead time is ~10-12 weeks including hire/installation for new racks in our colo. leases can be contracted in ~3-4 weeks for reserved racks from partner vendors. cloud rentals available in hours.

maya: so tradeoffs:
1) cloud rentals (spot + on-demand blend): fastest, flexible, but 30-40% higher unit $/GPU-hour at peak.
2) 6-12mo leases: middle ground, lower unit cost than cloud, faster than buys, but require contract and minimum commitment.
3) buy: lowest long-term cost but long lead time and capex hit.

raj: can we do hybrid — lease for APAC and buys for core US racks?

liam: technically yes, but buy order minimum is 16 GPUs per purchase unit (rack slice). mixing increases operational complexity (different kernel builds for NVLink config, different cooling). not impossible.

maya: quick cost sketch (very rough):
```
Lease (6mo avg): $0.55 / GPU-hour -> monthly per-8-gpu-slab ~ $3168
Cloud on-demand blend: $0.85 / GPU-hour -> monthly per-8-gpu-slab ~ $4896
Buy (amortized 36mo): $0.18 / GPU-hour -> monthly per-8-gpu-slab ~ $1036
```

elaine: finance note — those amortized numbers should include datacenter OPEX (power/cooling) + support. add ~12% on buy amortization.

maya: thanks, i'll inflate buy numbers by 12% for capacity comparison.

sergio: risk check: if we buy, supply chain for A100-class boards could slip. lead times reported by vendor= 22-30 weeks. that kills Q4 availability.

raj: so buy not viable for immediate Q4 surge unless we leverage existing inventory or move some non-critical workloads to preemptible instances.

liam: suggestion: mixed plan:
- short-term (next 8-12 weeks): ramp cloud rentals for burst windows, use aggressive prefix caching rule to reduce peak token load by ~12%
- mid-term (3-6 months): sign 6-9mo lease for eu-west + sg edge to guarantee latency-sensitive capacity
- long-term (9-18 months): evaluate buys for core us-west capacity when vendor ETAs firm up

maya: that matches my gut. cost-control knobs: tune batch sizes, increase KV cache TTL for common prefixes, and enable model-quantization on non-critical endpoints.

elaine: can you put a one-pager to finance with delta to plan vs. baseline and required capex/opex? they want numbers by EOB Fri.

maya: will do. putting preliminary ask here: 
- immediate cloud buffer: 1.2k GPUs-hours/day extra => est incremental $110k/month
- 6mo lease for eu & sg: ~64 GPUs total => est commit ~$460k over 6 months
- buy evaluation: placeholder 128 GPUs => est capex ~$1.5M (vendor TBD)

ops-bot: autoscaler alert — us-east-2 scaled +2 racks (16 GPUs) at 2026-04-01T09:12Z due to prefix cache miss burst.

sergio: note — networking: cross-region egress costs rise if we route APAC to EU/US frequently. suggest we model egress delta in the one-pager.

raj: also add sensitivity: 10/20/40% higher uptake scenarios and impact on reserve-era SLA (p99 latency).

maya: will include. final ask: quick thumbs? @raj @liam @elaine @sergio : do we go hybrid (cloud burst + leases) as preferred? :thumbsup: for yes, :thumbsdown: for no.

raj: :thumbsup:
liam: :thumbsup: but note automation + config work to keep parity across lease nodes.

elaine: :thumbsup: pending the one-pager numbers (finance sign-off).

sergio: :thumbsup:, but req ops runbook for lease fallback to cloud.

maya: great — i'll draft the one-pager and include a minimal runbook and a 6-week milestone plan. will ping when ready.

maya: quick followup — adding checklist for runbook:
- canonical inventory mapping (buy vs lease vs cloud)
- routing policy updates for latency-tiered customers
- autoscaler thresholds for burst windows (provision grace 12m)
- rollback plan to reduce cost if uptake stalls

liam: looks good. thanks everyone.

maya: thanks — closing thread for now, will post the doc here when ready.
